assessment.nobel_worthiness: Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics put electronic structure and nuclear motion into one simple, unified scheme, making ab initio simulation of condensed-phase, liquid, interfacial and biomolecular-adjacent systems routine. It is a real game-changer for how chemistry is simulated, with a direct line to modern ab initio MD, QM/MM and the data-generation side of machine-learned potentials. It sits naturally beside the 2013 recognition of multiscale modeling and the 1998 DFT prize while being a distinct methodological step.
assessment.attribution: The 1985 paper is a clean two-person invention, so the credit fits within a prize without strain. Parrinello is credited elsewhere on the list (metadynamics, ML potentials), but the decisive contribution here is the Car-Parrinello Lagrangian itself.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of continuous use, independent reimplementation in many codes and thousands of applications; no controversy over validity. Recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Some may argue Born-Oppenheimer MD with efficient DFT has partly displaced the original fictitious-dynamics scheme, which could blur the argument for lasting impact
Possible preference to bundle Parrinello's later work (metadynamics) instead; I have not verified how the committee would weigh that

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced proximity to degrade proteins is a genuinely new drug modality, converting binders into degraders and reaching undruggable targets. It has already produced clinical-stage molecules and a new understanding of how thalidomide-type drugs act. This meets the bar of something completely new with real consequences, and the chemistry (bifunctional design, ternary complex structure and cooperativity) is substantive.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies (with Sakamoto) made the first PROTAC concept; Ciulli contributed rational VHL ligand design and structural/mechanistic understanding of ternary complexes. The molecular-glue branch (Handa, Ito, Gray, others) is separate and the credit is split across more than three people, so a fair three-person configuration is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Concept is about 25 years old, clinical proof of concept is emerging but no PROTAC drug is yet widely approved; some recognition may be slightly early.
uncertainties: Pivotal clinical outcomes are still pending
Whether the prize should centre on PROTACs or on molecular glue degraders and cereblon biology
Sakamoto's role versus Deshaies is unclear to me and I cannot verify it

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskites turned a simple solution-processed material into a photovoltaic absorber approaching silicon efficiency within about a decade. It is a clear case of a surprising material class with huge scientific and technological reach, spanning defect tolerance, optoelectronics and LEDs.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka first used perovskites as sensitizers (2009); Park's 2012 solid-state cell and Snaith's mesostructured and planar devices established the field. Kanatzidis, Seok and Grätzel are also major contributors, so the three-person cut is contentious.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency and fundamental understanding are well established and widely reproduced, but long-term stability, lead toxicity and commercial viability remain open, so the consequences are not yet fully shown.
uncertainties: Stability and scale-up are unresolved
Priority and credit disputes among at least six credible people
Grätzel's dye-sensitized lineage complicates attribution

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Palladium-catalyzed C-N coupling gave a simple, general way to form aryl-nitrogen bonds and is used daily in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis. Its consequences are enormous and fully demonstrated, and the idea is the kind of simplifying tool that I value. It follows the 2010 cross-coupling prize but concerns a different bond construction and ligand design logic.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the catalyst systems and mechanistic understanding in the 1990s, building on Kosugi's and Migita's tin amide chemistry. Kosugi's precedent is a possible third name, but the decisive generality came from the two.
assessment.maturity: Extremely mature, with decades of independent use in industry and academia, so timing is not an issue.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize may count against it
Weight of Kosugi's earlier contribution is uncertain

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors perform defined chemical conversions on DNA bases without double-strand breaks, a conceptually clean design that combines protein evolution with nucleobase chemistry. It is already in clinical trials and widely used in research, a clear game-changer for genome engineering.
assessment.attribution: David R. Liu led the invention; Komor (cytosine base editor) and Gaudelli (adenine base editor) were the first-author contributors. Nishida and Kondo made an independent cytidine deaminase fusion, so there is a priority question. Prime editing (B035) is a related but separate Liu discovery, so any prize should be framed carefully.
assessment.maturity: Roughly a decade old, with early clinical results; independent confirmation is extensive, but long-term safety and efficacy outcomes are still accumulating. The 2020 CRISPR prize also leaves open whether this is too close.
uncertainties: Possible overlap with the CRISPR-Cas9 prize and a medicine-oriented reading
Whether a single-laureate prize (Liu alone) is more appropriate
Nishida and Kondo priority

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The funnel energy landscape view explained how proteins fold quickly despite astronomical conformational space, and linked theory to experiment through phi-value analysis. It strongly shaped how we think of folding, binding and function, and it matches my standard that theory must connect quantitatively to experiment. The AlphaFold prize (2024) addressed structure prediction, not the physical mechanism of folding, so this is complementary.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes, Onuchic and Bryngelson built the landscape theory; Fersht provided the experimental protein-engineering framework. Dill's contributions (hydrophobic collapse models) are also central, so the allocation is difficult and could appear arbitrary.
assessment.maturity: Decades of experimental and simulation support, with the funnel picture broadly accepted, although specific theoretical claims are still debated and the concept is more a framework than a single discovery.
uncertainties: Framing as a discovery rather than a conceptual framework
Difficult credit among five or more people, including Dill
Possible concern that a 2024 protein-structure prize makes this less pressing

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs allow site-specific incorporation of designed noncanonical amino acids in living cells and organisms, extending the genetic code. It is a general, enabling tool for protein chemistry and biology, with applications in therapeutics and mechanistic enzymology, and it has demonstrated a broad range of consequences.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang established the first eukaryotic and bacterial systems; Chin generalized to eukaryotes and multicellular organisms and to quadruplet and multi-site recoding. Mehl and Yokoyama contributed as well, so the three-person cut leaves out credible people.
assessment.maturity: More than 20 years of independent validation across many laboratories; the technology is mature, although therapeutic translation is still limited.
uncertainties: Choice among Schultz, Chin, Wang, Mehl and Yokoyama is contestable
Whether the work is judged as chemistry or as biology

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantitative mass-spectrometry proteomics transformed biochemistry by allowing systematic, large-scale measurement of proteins, modifications and interactions. The practical consequences across cell biology and medicine are substantial and long demonstrated.
assessment.attribution: Mann, Aebersold and Yates are the leading figures for high-accuracy MS proteomics, isotope-coded quantification and shotgun proteomics respectively. Gygi, Hunt and Heck are also major contributors, and soft ionization was already honored in 2002, so this builds on earlier prizes.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with widespread independent use and consensus on its importance.
uncertainties: Field is a broad toolbox rather than a single discovery, so the prize motivation may be diffuse
Strong competing candidates within the same list for the credit (Hunt, Gygi, Heck)
